post.description: Pairs this browser with a code from a trusted client, and sets its token cookie.
A one-time code for pairing another device.

get.description:
Everything that changes while no run is open: memory, skills, jobs, integrations, runs
started from other channels. Clients keep this open for their whole session, so it also
tells which clients are connected. A new connection starts from now; a reconnection sends
the last id it received and gets what it missed.

post.description: A new conversation for the calling client, which leaves the one it was on.

put.description: Replaces one profile section with the user's own list. 422: an unknown section or too many items.

schema.title: Response Conversation Messages Conversations  Thread Id  Messages Get

post.description: Moves the calling client to an earlier conversation, leaving the one it was on.

delete.description:
Deletes a conversation no client is on. 404: no such conversation; 409: a client is on
it or a reply is running.

get.description: The files the user sent in their conversations, newest first.

post.description: The reply as an OGG Opus voice note when Settings → Audio speaks it, else 204.

schema.title: Response Channel Waiting Channels  Name  Approvals Get

get.description: The presets of the email plugins that are on.

schema.title: Response Email Providers Integrations Email Providers Get
Response Email Accounts Integrations Email Accounts Get

post.description: Checks the logins with the servers first. The first account becomes the default.

The provider's sign-in page; the browser comes back to `redirect_uri`. 400: unknown
provider or missing values. 404: unknown account.

put.description: Only the name; the sign-in stays.

get.description: Who the agent may email without asking, from any account, besides the user's own accounts.

post.description:
The last step of a sign-in (an email account, a remote MCP server). Open to unpaired
browsers: the one-time state is the proof (the web app's /app/oauth page may be opened on
the daemon's own computer, before pairing). 400: expired state, refused code, or a server
that won't work with the tokens.

put.description: 404: no such skill. 400: built in, or the text is empty.

delete.description: 404: no such skill. 400: built in, or it comes with an MCP server.

post.description:
Install the skill again from its repository. 404: no such skill. 400: not installed, or
the repository can't be read.

schema.title: Response Mcp Servers Mcp Servers Get

post.description:
Connect once and list the server's tools, without saving it. A remote server may ask to
sign in instead: it can be added, then signed in to.

delete.description: With `delete_data`, the server's data folder goes too; otherwise it stays.

post.description:
The server's sign-in page; the browser comes back to `redirect_uri`, which finishes it
(/oauth/finish). 404: no such server. 400: a local server, one that can't be reached or
doesn't ask to sign in.

Install the server again from its repository. 404: no such server. 400: not installed
from one, the repository can't be read, or the new version needs a value not given yet.

get.description: MCP servers and skills that keep failing, the newest first.

Installed plugins the extras have a newer version of, as of the last check. Empty while
checks are off.

schema.title: Response Plugin Updates Repositories Updates Get

post.description: The skills and MCP servers a git repository offers. 400: it can't be read or has none.
400: the repository can't be read, lacks something picked, a name is taken, or a field is empty.
The text read aloud on this host (Kokoro), as WAV.

schema.title: Response Model Providers Settings Model Providers Get

put.description: Checks that both models answer with these settings, then uses them.

get.description: Tokens and cost of the model calls, by day, model, purpose, channel, conversation, job, skill and tool.

ConnectedClient.title: ConnectedClient
ConnectedClient.description:
A client holding the daemon's event stream open. `transport` is "unix socket" or host:port.
`device_id` is the paired device it connected from (empty on the Unix socket), `thread_id` the
conversation it's on (empty until it starts, resumes or writes to one).

FoundServer.title: FoundServer
FoundServer.description: An MCP server in a repository, before it's installed.

FoundSkill.title: FoundSkill
FoundSkill.description: A skill in a repository, before it's installed.

McpServerChange.title: McpServerChange
McpServerChange.description: Fields to change; the ones left out keep their value.

McpServerStatus.title: McpServerStatus
McpServerStatus.description: What a client shows. Has the names of env values and headers, never the values.

Me.title: Me
Me.description: The caller: a trusted client (Unix socket), or the paired device it is.

MemorySnapshot.title: MemorySnapshot
MemorySnapshot.description: What the assistant currently knows about the user, in plain types for gateways.

ModelProvider.title: ModelProvider
ModelProvider.description: A provider clients offer, with what it asks for and the models to suggest.

ModelStatus.title: ModelStatus
ModelStatus.description: What a client shows. Says which secret values are set, never the values.

ServerField.title: ServerField
ServerField.description: A value the user gives when installing: an env value of a local server, a header of a remote one.

SetupItem.title: SetupItem
SetupItem.description:
A line the apps show for a channel: text, a code to read out, a value to copy, or a button
(`value` is the action it sends back).

SpeechStatus.title: SpeechStatus
SpeechStatus.description: The chosen settings and what can be chosen.

StartupStatus.title: StartupStatus
StartupStatus.description: Whether the daemon starts at boot, and whether this daemon was started that way.

TokenRow.title: TokenRow
TokenRow.description:
Tokens of one day, model, conversation, tool... `cost` in US dollars, None when no model
involved has a price (core/usage/prices.py).

WebSearchStatus.title: WebSearchStatus
WebSearchStatus.description: What a settings screen shows. Never includes the key.
